questions.question: Where does the subclavius muscle lie in relation to the clavicle?
questions.explanation: The subclavius is a small rounded muscle that lies horizontally inferior to the clavicle.

questions.question: From which structure does the subclavius muscle originate?
options: First rib at the costochondral junction
Second rib at the costochondral junction
questions.explanation: It arises from the first rib at the costochondral junction.

questions.question: Into which structure does the subclavius muscle insert?
questions.explanation: Subclavius is inserted into the subclavian groove on the inferior surface of the clavicle.

questions.question: Which nerve supplies the subclavius muscle?
questions.explanation: It is supplied by the nerve to subclavius from the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.

questions.question: The nerve to subclavius arises from which part of the brachial plexus?
questions.explanation: The nerve to subclavius arises from the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.

questions.question: What is the main action of the subclavius muscle?
questions.explanation: The subclavius stabilizes the clavicle by pulling it inferiorly and medially.

questions.question: Which muscle is described as a broad sheet that clothes the side wall of the thorax?
questions.explanation: The serratus anterior is a broad sheet of muscle that clothes the side wall of the thorax.

questions.question: From how many ribs does the serratus anterior arise?
questions.explanation: It arises by a series of 8 digitations from the upper eight ribs.

questions.question: Which ribs give rise to the first digitation of the serratus anterior?
questions.explanation: The first digitation arises from the 1st and 2nd ribs.

questions.question: Where is the serratus anterior inserted?
questions.explanation: It is inserted into the costal surface of the scapula along its medial border.

questions.question: Which nerve supplies the serratus anterior?
questions.explanation: It is supplied by the long thoracic nerve (C5, C6, and C7).

questions.question: Which spinal roots contribute to the long thoracic nerve?
questions.explanation: The long thoracic nerve carries fibers from C5, C6, and C7.

questions.question: The serratus anterior is also called the boxer's muscle because it performs which action?
questions.explanation: It pulls the scapula forward for pushing and punching movements as required during boxing.

questions.question: The lower 4 or 5 digitations of the serratus anterior rotate the scapula in which direction?
questions.explanation: Its lower 4 or 5 digitations rotate the scapula laterally and upwards during overhead abduction.

questions.question: Paralysis of the serratus anterior leads to which clinical condition?
questions.explanation: Paralysis leads to a condition called winging of the scapula.

questions.question: Which structure is continuous inferiorly with the pectoral fascia?
options: Investing layer of deep cervical fascia
questions.explanation: Inferiorly, the pectoral fascia is continuous with the fascia of the anterior abdominal wall.

questions.question: The pectoral fascia is continuous superolaterally with the fascia covering which muscle?
questions.explanation: It passes over the deltopectoral groove to become continuous with the fascia covering the deltoid muscle.

questions.question: The clavipectoral fascia fills the space between the clavicle and which muscle?
questions.explanation: It fills the space between the clavicle and the pectoralis minor muscle.

questions.question: Which muscle is enclosed by the upper part of the clavipectoral fascia?
questions.explanation: The upper part of the clavipectoral fascia splits into two laminae to enclose the subclavius muscle.

questions.question: Which muscle is enclosed by the lower part of the clavipectoral fascia?
questions.explanation: Its lower part splits to enclose the pectoralis minor muscle.

questions.question: Below the pectoralis minor, the clavipectoral fascia extends downwards as what structure?
questions.explanation: It extends downwards as the suspensory ligament of axilla, which is attached to the dome of the axillary fascia.

questions.question: What is the function of the suspensory ligament of axilla?
questions.explanation: It keeps the dome of axillary fascia pulled up, thus maintaining the concavity of the axilla.

questions.question: The thick upper part of the clavipectoral fascia is called what?
questions.explanation: The thick upper part extending from the first rib to the coracoid process is called the costocoracoid ligament.

questions.question: Which nerve pierces the clavipectoral fascia?
questions.explanation: The lateral pectoral nerve is one of the four structures that pierce the clavipectoral fascia.

questions.question: Which artery pierces the clavipectoral fascia?
questions.explanation: The thoraco-acromial artery pierces the clavipectoral fascia.

questions.question: Which vein pierces the clavipectoral fascia?
questions.explanation: The cephalic vein pierces the clavipectoral fascia.

questions.question: The lymphatics piercing the clavipectoral fascia drain to which group of nodes?
questions.explanation: Lymphatics from the breast pierce the fascia to reach the apical group of axillary lymph nodes.

questions.question: Which two structures pass outwards after piercing the clavipectoral fascia?
options: Lateral pectoral nerve and thoraco-acromial artery
Medial pectoral nerve and axillary artery
questions.explanation: The lateral pectoral nerve and thoraco-acromial artery pass outwards, while the other two pass inwards.

questions.question: Which two structures pass inwards after piercing the clavipectoral fascia?
options: Lateral pectoral nerve and thoraco-acromial artery
Long thoracic nerve and thoracodorsal artery
questions.explanation: The lymphatics and cephalic vein pass inwards through the clavipectoral fascia.

questions.question: Which structure does the pectoral fascia become continuous with inferolaterally?
questions.explanation: Inferolaterally, it curves round the inferolateral border of the pectoralis major to become continuous with the axillary fascia.
